video.title: The Beginner-Friendly Claude AI Side Hustle Nobody Talks About

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Ryan Dozer, a solo AI marketer who runs a six-figure SEO/content agency. Dozer explains Claude skills (markdown SOPs for AI agents) and how he packaged about 20-25 of his own into a $99 'Claude Code skill stack' sold from his own site via Stripe, claiming over $3,000 in 30-45 days. He demonstrates an SEO blog-post-writer skill that turns YouTube videos into ranking articles, a LinkedIn scraper skill using Apify, and a vibe-coded marketing OS. Key takeaway: turn the workflows and expertise you already use daily into skills and sell them as digital products, but the numbers are self-reported and the sales path leans on his existing audience.

speakers.name: Ryan Dozer
speakers.description: AI marketer who runs a solo six-figure SEO/content marketing agency and sells Claude skills

ideas.name: Claude Code skill stack digital product
ideas.one_liner: Package your own working Claude skills (markdown SOP files) and sell them as a downloadable bundle for $99.
ideas.business_model: One-off digital product sales via own website and Stripe, promoted by soft-sell CTAs in content and email
ideas.customer: Marketers and power users of Claude Code, Codex or other AI agents who want ready-made skills
ideas.problem: Users must build their own prompts and SOPs for AI agents and copy-paste between GPTs and projects, which is tedious
ideas.offer: Bundle of about 20-25 markdown skill files (SEO blog post writer, YouTube thumbnail designer, anti-slop skill, web designer etc.) plus Claude.md tips, delivered as downloads

pricing.notes: One sale came from a $1,000 one-hour consulting upsell, so not all revenue was $99 sales.

acquisition_channels.details: Blog posts and a new SEO test site gaining traffic from Google and LLMs, with a floating popup and CTAs in blog posts
CTAs in email newsletters and drip sequences; YouTube channel and community (AI Marketing Insiders)
Videos are repurposed into SEO blog posts that link back to the product

ideas.delivery: Customer gets a page with download links to markdown files, then repurposes them with their own context. Fully digital, no human delivery per sale.
unit_economics_claims: Over $3,000 in 30-45 days, described as passive
Only Stripe fees (about 3%) as cost, plus his time
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated beyond existing Claude subscription and time; landing page built in about 15-20 minutes with Claude Code
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Launched about 30-45 days before recording and already over $3,000

acquisition.how: SEO blog posts, email drips and popups can be agent-produced, but the traffic relies on the founder's existing audience and authority.

onboarding.how: Purchase leads straight to a download page.

support.how: Low volume; an FAQ and an agent for emails, with occasional human help. Skills may need updates as models change.

uk_applicability.notes: Digital product sold via Stripe works the same in the UK; VAT and digital-services rules apply.

risks: Revenue is self-reported and partly a $1,000 consulting upsell
Skills are easily copied or replaced by Anthropic's free skills
Sales depend on an existing audience
Model and platform changes can make skills obsolete
Low price point needs sustained traffic

tactics.name: Convert a Claude project into a skill
steps: Install Anthropic's free skill creator skill from their GitHub
Open the project and voice-dump an instruction to repurpose the project into a skill markdown file, keeping instructions, memory and recent chat history
Refine the output, then download the markdown file
Use it in the web app or move it to another AI agent

quote.text: use the skill creator skill to transform or repurpose this project into a into a skill markdown file
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Granular one-skill-per-task design
steps: Create one skill per task (SEO blog writer, newsletter writer, sales email writer)
Tell the skill to update itself when you correct mistakes

quote.text: I have one clawed skill per marketing task.
quote.speaker: Ryan Dozer

tactics.name: Build the sales page with your own skills
steps: Give it to Claude Code with a web designer skill that knows branding, tone and logo
Add social proof and FAQs; page done in about 15-20 minutes
Promote with a floating popup, blog CTAs and email/drip CTAs, soft sell

quote.text: in about 15 20 minutes this Claude Code skill stack was complete.
quote.speaker: Ryan Dozer

tactics.name: Dogfooding content flywheel
steps: Use your skills to produce SEO content
Ship content to a site that sells the same skill stack
Add soft CTAs in posts and emails

tactics.name: Reduce AI hallucination with a check line
steps: End skill prompts with an instruction to triple check the skill instructions
Give the model keywords and exact link lists

quote.text: Triple check the SEO blog post writer instructions when doing this task

lessons.lesson: Monetise workflows you already use daily; building for yourself first gives a validated product and better client work.

quote.text: I'm not just selling these as a digital product, Chris. I'm actually using these in my day-to-day work.
quote.speaker: Ryan Dozer

lessons.lesson: Sell into smaller, less crowded marketplaces and ecosystems rather than the crowded main app stores.
Portable, plain-text skills protect against platform lock-in because they transfer across AI agents.
Expertise in any niche can become a product, not just marketing.
Soft-sell CTAs across content, email and drip sequences can sell a low-priced digital product without hard pushing.
Use AI to build your landing page and payment flow quickly, cutting launch time to minutes.
Skills turn into consulting upsells; a product can open high-value service conversations.
Move from copy-paste chat workflows to agentic tools and learn them through daily tasks.

quote.text: Figure out what are my tasks that I'm doing every day
quote.speaker: Ryan Dozer

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with a Stripe dashboard shown on screen, but $3,000 is a modest, self-reported total, partly a $1,000 consulting sale, and traffic and conversion data are vague. Sales lean on his existing audience; claims of 'passive' income are unverified.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Dozer sells the $99 skill stack and promotes his community and site; the video includes a Go High Level sponsor read.
